title: Correct metering for stacked impersonation and project-alias handoff
creator: Asha Patel
description: Background: We are seeing intermittent billing and quota attribution drift when requests flow through a chain of service-account impersonation + project alias rewrites (common for enterprise customers using cross-project routing and proxying). Symptoms: usage is attributed to the upstream caller org or a canonical project alias instead of the final impersonated project, causing both overcharges on the caller and under-reporting on the target project. This ticket scopes the investigation, fix, and backfill plan to ensure deterministic attribution for stacked impersonation flows.
steps_to_reproduce: Create two projects: provider-project and tenant-project; configure a proxy service in provider-project that impersonates a service account in tenant-project.
Register an API key associated with provider-project and set up a project alias mapping for tenant-project (alias -> canonical-project-id).

Send a burst of generation requests through the proxy using the provider API key where proxy performs service-account impersonation header (x-impersonate: sa@tenant) and rewrites project header to alias.
Observe usage events in kafka/ingress topic and check metering pipeline attribution as recorded in billing-snapshots and quota counters.
Repeat while rotating the proxy's API key within a <60s window to increase chance of cache invalidation and race conditions.
Expected: all tokens and events should attribute to tenant-project (final impersonated principal). Observed: a subset attributed to provider-project or to the alias canonical id incorrectly.
observed_behavior: Intermittent spikes where provider-project shows extra tokens consumed while tenant-project shows deficit
Rate limiter counters increment on provider-project leading to unexpected 429s
Backfill reconciliation detects ghost usage windows spanning token rotations
expected_behavior: All usage from the impersonation chain should be attributed to the final impersonated project/service account
Rate limits applied against the effective project, not the initial caller, when impersonation semantics indicate delegation
No double-counting or ghost billing windows introduced by API key rotation during active sessions
investigation_notes: Initial logs: identity-claim resolution uses cached alias->project mapping at event-emission time; when token rotation occurs, some events are emitted using the pre-rotation claim leading to mixed attribution.

Trace of a failing request: ingress proxy authenticates key (provider), issues a short-lived impersonation token for tenant SA, but event enrichment pipeline re-hydrates project from original apiKey record before impersonation claim is applied.
Metering pipeline attaches 'effective_principal' using auth-context snapshot; snapshot timing currently captured at 'authenticate' stage, not after impersonation reconciliation.
Reproducer on staging: enabling 'auth.debug' shows two distinct emit events for same trace id with different project ids separated by ~40ms.
root_cause_summary: Attribution resolution happens from an auth snapshot taken before the impersonation/alias normalization completes. Race with API key rotation and cache expiry causes some events to carry stale project identifiers. The metering path lacks an idempotent override from the final impersonation claim.
proposed_fix: Move effective-principal resolution to after impersonation/alias normalization in the auth pipeline; ensure a single canonical 'attribution' header is injected into the request context before any metering emission points.
Introduce a short-lived write-through cache for alias->project mapping that is updated synchronously on token swap to reduce window-of-inconsistency.
Add an explicit metadata flag on usage events: 'final_impersonation_principal' that the metering pipeline prefers over any pre-existing project fields if present.
Add end-to-end integration tests simulating token rotation + alias rewrites and a stress test to ensure no race reproduces at 10k req/s.
migration_backfill: Run a reconciling job that scans suspect windows (identified by traces with multi-principal events) and rewrites billing snapshots to the final_impersonation_principal when determinable.
Backfill will be run in read-only analysis mode first to estimate customer deltas; follow up with an opt-in write-back phase and an audit report for finance.
Provide a reconciliation window cutoff of 90 days scoped to enterprise customers with reported anomalies.
rollout_plan: Implement feature behind 'attribution-after-impersonation' feature flag in auth-service and metering-service.
Canary on 5% of hosted API traffic for 48 hours; monitor billing deltas, 429s and error rates.
If stable, expand to 25% for 24 hours, then 100% rollout.
Coordinate with finance to hold off billing exports until backfill audit completes to avoid customer-facing mismatches.
qa_checks: Unit tests for alias normalization and final_principal precedence
Integration test that verifies single attribution per trace id under token rotation stress
Load test at 10k rps for 30m confirming no attribution flip-flops
Manual verification: run sample enterprise repro and validate billing snapshots and quota counters match expected target project
monitoring_and_alerting: Create temporary alert 'billing.attribution.flipflop.rate' when >0.1% of traces have multiple project ids within 60s
Dashboard: per-project delta between ingress-metered and billing-snapshots to surface sudden shifts
Audit log capture for all reconciliation writes with actor and diff summary
